KEY MESSAGE 1...Primarily dry weather is expected through this Sunday, 
but periodic rain showers are possible this Thursday evening 
through Thursday night and again this Sunday. Near-record warmth
is forecast this Thursday.

A surface ridge continues to affect our region today through
tonight as the embedded high pressure center moves SE'ward from
northern ON toward northern New England, while the ridge aloft 
builds from the Upper Midwest to the eastern Great Lakes. Dry 
weather is expected as stabilizing subsidence accompanies the 
ridge. Widespread low-level clouds, which appear to be 
associated with moist isentropic ascent ahead of a 925-700 mb 
shortwave trough axis oriented generally from WSW to ENE and 
embedded in NW'erly mean flow in that atmospheric layer, should 
exit our CWA generally from north to south through daybreak this
morning. Sufficient cloud breaks and weak or calm surface winds
should contribute to localized steam fog in the Black River 
Valley and the inland lake and river valleys of the Western 
Southern Tier and Finger Lakes Region during the predawn hours 
through about 10 AM EDT today. However, a NE'erly to ENE'erly 
mean flow in the surface to 925 mb layer and weak lake-induced 
instability amidst limited synoptic-scale low-level moisture 
over ~14C Lake America, should allow scattered to perhaps 
widespread and shallow lake-effect stratocumuli to impact 
portions of Western and Central NY, especially metro Rochester 
and the northern Finger Lakes Region, through mid-morning. 
These lake-effect clouds should then dissipate by midday as 
lake-induced CAPE dissipates via low-level dry air advection 
and a lowering subsidence inversion.
 
Lows are still expected to reach mainly the 20's to mid 30's 
around daybreak this morning and be followed by highs in the mid
40's to lower 60's late late this afternoon as low-level CAA 
persists behind yesterday's cold front passage. Weak or calm 
surface winds, low humidity, and sufficient cloud breaks, 
especially farther east, are expected to permit appreciable 
radiational cooling very late this afternoon through daybreak 
Wednesday. Lows should reach mainly the lower 20's to lower 
30's in North-Central NY and the lower 30's to lower 40's 
elsewhere in our CWA around daybreak Wednesday.

On Wednesday through Wednesday night, the ridge at the surface 
and aloft should exit E'ward and allow a warm front starved of 
low-level moisture to sweep NE'ward through our region and 
usher-in a somewhat warmer air mass. Fair weather is expected to
persist. Late afternoon highs should reach the 50's to lower 
60's in North-Central NY and the upper 50's to upper 60's 
elsewhere in our CWA. Thereafter, overnight lows should reach 
the mid 30's to mid 40's in North-Central NY and the lower 40's
to lower 50's elsewhere in our CWA around daybreak Thursday. 

Mainly W'erly to WNW'erly flow aloft and a series of attendant 
troughs and ridges at the surface and aloft should affect our 
region this Thursday through upcoming weekend. Current odds 
favor primarily dry weather as ridging should affect Western and
Central NY during the majority of the time period. However, a 
weak cold front should sweep E'ward through our region Thursday 
night. Periodic rain showers should impact Western and Central 
NY Thursday evening and especially Thursday night, along and 
ahead of the front, due to moist isentropic ascent ahead of a 
shortwave trough axis aloft and low-level convergence/ascent 
along the front coinciding with sufficient low-level moisture. 
Additional periodic rain showers are possible this Sunday due to
moist isentropic ascent preceding another shortwave trough axis
aloft. Unusually-mild weather for late October is expected on 
Thursday through this weekend courtesy of largely zonal flow 
aloft. For example, near-record warm highs in the upper 60's to
mid 70's are expected in many lower elevation locations in our 
Western NY and Finger Lakes counties this Thursday afternoon, 
including the Buffalo and Rochester metro areas.
